Every public course-material site I maintain, together with the graduate
courses whose materials are still being built. Undergraduate and graduate
records sit in one inventory rather than in separate catalogs, grouped by what
the courses are about.

Only records that link out have a public course site. A course whose materials
are in development, and a planning-stage curriculum direction, are shown as
plain text with nothing to click — see [what the statuses
mean](#what-the-statuses-mean) below.

## What the statuses mean {#what-the-statuses-mean}

Status describes the **public materials**, not whether a course exists.

- **Current offering** — tied to a presently scheduled section.
- **Maintained public reference** — a durable, public resource collection that
  is not currently representing a scheduled section. Dates, weights, and final
  policies are not set here.
- **In development** — materials are still being assembled, so dates,
  policies, assessments, and readings remain provisional.
- **No public materials yet** — the course is real and established, but
  nothing public exists for it.
- **Curriculum direction** — a planning-stage area of the curriculum. Not a
  scheduled course, not an adopted requirement, and not an in-development
  course site.

Anything operational for a live section — meetings, dates, assessments,
grades, and announcements — belongs in the LMS, not here.

See the [Teaching overview](teaching.qmd) for current courses, the teaching
approach, the Course Builder harness, and the Math Assistance Center.
